A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original Gaussian-mixture transport experiments measuring map errors as training sample counts and network widths vary (Section 5, Figures 3–4).

after.justification: V4 retains those experiments and adds original baseline comparisons, higher-dimensional results, and visualizations of learned maps in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Theorem 4.3 replaces the raw neural-map construction with networks composed with projection onto Y, adding an output operation to the theoretical model class. The minimax objective and reported experimental training procedure are retained; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 extends evaluation from dimensions 2 and 4 to 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128. This expands dimensional coverage within the retained synthetic Gaussian-mixture transport task.

E2.justification: V3 provides no direct empirical comparison with other estimators. V4 introduces a comparison against mean-shift, constant, and linear estimators in Appendix C.1 and Figure 5, substantially expanding the comparator coverage.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve sample-count ranges, error metrics, regression procedures, optimization budgets, batch sizes, and 4096 test samples. Appendix C follows the existing Section 5 settings. The newly disclosed repeated-run practice belongs to E5.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds dimension-sensitivity analysis and a focused case study visualizing collapsing solutions at narrow potential widths. These extend the existing estimation-error and width analyses; the original width-ablation results remain.

E5.justification: V4 Appendix D newly states that experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.2 use three different random seeds and report mean errors. V3 does not specify this practice. This establishes new reporting, not an increase in runs; neither version provides confidence intervals or error bars.

E6.justification: Figures 3–4 retain their results, while Figures 5–7 add baseline curves, five higher-dimensional convergence studies, and qualitative map outcomes. Figure 6 reports slopes including −0.235 at dimension 16 and −0.583 at dimension 128. These are substantial new results under added conditions, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: V4 adds convex-support assumptions and sufficient density conditions for strong convexity in Remark 4.8. New Lemma A.7 proves projection nonexpansiveness, and Appendices A.3/A.5 incorporate projection into approximation and Rademacher arguments. Appendix A.5 also corrects epsilon scaling for the 4/beta factor. These substantively revise the foundations of the retained bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: error decomposition, Rademacher-based estimation bounds, approximation guarantees, and learnability for quadratic minimax OT. The additional experiments do not introduce a new headline contribution.

C2.justification: V4 explains nonuniform higher-dimensional convergence through the distinction between bounds and observed rates, with possible optimization effects. It also attributes narrow-network collapse to limited expressivity and discusses distributions intended to satisfy strong convexity. The existing main limitations remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds a code URL, identifies PyTorch, states supplementary-code availability, and documents the new baseline estimators. Existing hardware, optimizer, training-budget, and testing details move from Appendix C to D without substantive changes. Actual online availability was not checked.

R1.justification: V4 adds Caffarelli (1996), Gushchin et al. (2023), Kolesov et al. (2024b), and Nietert and Goldfeld (2025), with limited additional positioning. Divol et al.'s publication update refers to the same work. The main distinction from non-minimax OT and GAN analyses remains.

P1.justification: V4 streamlines Section 2 around quadratic duality, polishes wording, updates author/header text, and adds reproducibility and acknowledgment passages. A new experimental appendix shifts the retained implementation, GAN, and LLM-usage appendices. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain.

P2.justification: New Figures 5–7 substantially expand the visual evidence with baseline comparisons, higher-dimensional convergence panels, and input/target/learned-map visualizations. Figure 4 is redrawn with actual width labels 1, 2, 4, and 8. Figure 3 moves, while Figures 1–3 retain identical image content.

improvement.justification: V4 improves mathematical support through projection handling and corrected epsilon scaling, adds useful diagnostic evidence, and improves reproducibility disclosures. These strengthen the retained contribution. A small countervailing issue is that Appendix C.1's blanket baseline-superiority wording exceeds Figure 5's evidence at the smallest 4D sample size.
